svg.title: Skills-based hiring reached fewer than one in 700 US hires in 2023
svg.desc: A grid of 700 dots representing US hires, with one dot highlighted: Burning Glass Institute and Harvard Business School estimate that removing degree requirements created new opportunity for about 97,000 workers out of 77 million annual hires, a net 0.14 percentage points. A lower bar splits firms that dropped requirements into 37 percent that changed hiring, 45 percent that changed only the posting, and about 18 percent that ended up hiring fewer non-degreed workers.
svg.text: Dropping degree requirements changed fewer than one hire in 700
Each dot is one US hire in 2023. The dark dot is the share newly reachable because an employer dropped a degree requirement.
a net shift of 0.14 percentage points
FIRMS THAT DROPPED A REQUIREMENT, BY WHAT THEY ACTUALLY DID
